release: 2026-10-28 Sovereign / interpretive Aramaic-sensitive Lord's Prayer / Genesis side FINAL

changes.original: YHWH Elohim caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As he slept, YHWH Elohim took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
changes.final: YHWH Elohim caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As he slept, YHWH Elohim took one of his sides, and closed up the flesh in its place.
changes.rationale: Hebrew tsela more broadly side; rib possible narrower sense but not certain. Preserve October 15 man/human decision and sleep/flesh imagery.

changes.original: YHWH Elohim made a woman from the rib which YHWH Elohim had taken from the man, and brought her to him.
changes.final: YHWH Elohim fashioned the side that had been taken from the man into a woman, and brought her to him.
changes.rationale: Hebrew tsela side; banah conveys building/fashioning. 'Eve' naming is later, Genesis 3:20.

methodology: Peshitta Syriac Aramaic is a historical witness, not verifiable verbatim Galilean Aramaic.
Neil Douglas-Klotz Prayers of the Cosmos is interpretive poetic inspiration, not the exact lexical meaning of the Syriac.
Literal Greek/Syriac senses retained where practical; inner insight, purpose, mistakes binding, unripeness, surface delusion are intentional interpretive expansions.
King of Judeans historical inscriptions and political quotations are unchanged; God already Sovereign in previous editorial release.
Genesis side stage is LAST for current public canonical release and most recent public change-log entry.
